subject: Meridian Health — segmentation of processing roles and key custody for private deployment
messages:
From: Legal - Meridian Health <legal@meridianhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Questions on private deployment — key custody & operator access

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Meridian legal has a few follow-ups as we evaluate a private (VPC) deployment:

1) Key custody: we need confirmation on whether customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-keys) means Redwood will have any form of administrative access to customer key material or key metadata.
2) Operator access scope: please confirm what level of operator (Redwood) access is required for routine maintenance vs. break-glass emergencies. We need tight boundaries in the DPA.
3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfer: we require a current list of subprocessors that would touch encrypted customer data (if any), and the mechanism for restricting transfers outside the US.

Can you also send any network diagrams or a redline of the standard DPA reflecting private deployment options? We may want to propose specific language for operator access audits.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30-minute call with our InfoSec team next week.

— Rajiv Singh
Sr. Counsel, Meridian Health
legal@meridianhealth.com
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Legal - Meridian Health <legal@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment — key custody & operator access

Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled together short answers below and attached two items you requested (a redlined DPA and an updated network diagram). Happy to walk through on a call — I can propose slots after the bullet section.

Summary answers (high level):
- Customer-managed KMS: In our private deployment offering you retain exclusive control of your key material. Redwood never receives plaintext keys or key material. We support customer KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM) and a customer key-wrapping configuration.
- Operator access: Routine maintenance does not require access to customer plaintext data or keys. Break-glass is limited to a narrowly defined emergency procedure: access is ephemeral, auditable, and requires (1) customer emergency approval via a designated channel OR (2) dual-authorization from our security and your on-call contact if the customer is unreachable. All break-glass activity is logged and recorded.
- Subprocessors & transfers: For the private (VPC/on-prem) model, the set of subprocessors is small and largely limited to cloud infra partners for hosting (if any). If processing is fully on-prem with customer hardware, there are zero Redwood subprocessors touching the data plane. We will supply a subprocessor list and execute territorial restrictions per the DPA.

Attachments included: DPA_redlined_v3.docx (redline suggested language for key custody + operator access), meridian_network_diagram_v2.pdf (shows control-plane separation and optional air-gapped flow).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop in Vivian (security) and Monica (privacy) for suggested DPA language — Monica, any quick notes to add?
- Rajiv, would you prefer Wed 12/3 or Thu 12/4 for a 30-minute call with InfoSec?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Architect — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, legal@meridianhealth.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment — key custody & operator access

Quick privacy notes (flagging suggested DPA language):
- Key custody clause: propose a clause that explicitly states "Redwood shall have no access to customer plaintext keys or encrypted data when customer-managed KMS is used; any key escrow or split-escrow arrangement must be explicitly documented and mutually agreed."
- Operator access: add a requirement that all break-glass sessions are recorded, signed off within 24 hours by a named Meridian contact, and limited to console-level commands (no ability to export raw token logs).
- Subprocessor list: provide an addendum that is updated quarterly and available via a secure link — include a right for the customer to object/remove a subprocessor with rollback timeline.

Also recommending we pre-authorize a short emergency playbook that lists who at Meridian can give emergency consent (name + contact) — saves time in outages.

— Monica Patel
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Legal - Meridian Health <legal@meridianhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment — key custody & operator access

Thanks Grace / Monica — that read helps. A couple follow-ups before the call: 

1) Can you confirm whether any operational telemetry (e.g., agent heartbeats, health pings) includes metadata that would allow Redwood to reconstruct or infer data residency or dataset identifiers? We need assurance that metadata cannot be used to correlate patient volumes to regions.
2) For break-glass: what is the retention period for logs and session recordings? Our policy requires 7 years for auditability in regulated contexts.

If you can confirm the retention policy and provide the current subprocessors with country locations, we can prepare a short redline back and then schedule the call.

— Rajiv
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: legal@meridianhealth.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 15:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment — key custody & operator access

Rajiv — quick technical clarifications from infra/security that should address the last points: 

- Telemetry & metadata: Health pings are strictly operational and do not include dataset identifiers or patient counts. We only collect anonymized service metrics (cpu/mem/queue depth/request latency) and a hashed service instance id; hashed ids are rotated regularly. There is no tenant-specific dataset pointer included in telemetry.
- Log/session retention: Break-glass session recordings and audit logs are retained for 7 years by default in our enterprise private package (we can also offer a shorter retention via contract if required). Logs are stored encrypted with customer-controlled keys where configured.
- Subprocessors: Attached is a current minimal list (infra-provider-us-east, backup-svc-partner) and their primary processing country. If Meridian is fully on-prem, we will mark subprocessors as "none" for the data plane in the DPA.

Linking our internal ticket for traceability: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9243 (contains the redline language and action items).

If that works, Grace — please propose the call slots and I’ll join to support any live technical questions.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
